title: A Local Certificate for the Zeros of the Riemann Zeta Function from a Mixed Boundary Problem
content: On the critical line the functional equation gives the normal derivative of \( \log|\zeta| \): it is \( \pi \) times the sum of the Dirac masses at the sign changes of Hardy's function Z, minus an explicit archimedean term. On \( \operatorname{Re}s=\frac32 \) the Euler product gives \( \log|\zeta| \) and its normal derivative. The mixed (Dirichlet--Neumann) problem in the strip \( \frac12<\operatorname{Re}s<\frac32 \) is therefore well posed, and the defect of its prediction is the explicit formula with the test function \( \frac\pi2\operatorname{sech}\frac{\pi x}2 \), minus the sign changes. We show that this defect is a sum of nonnegative terms, one for every zero that is not a sign change, and that an off-line pair at depth \( \delta \) contributes the kernel \( 2\pi\cos\frac{\pi\delta}2\cosh\frac{\pi x}2/(\cosh\pi x+\cos\pi\delta) \), whose peak is \( \pi/\cos\frac{\pi\delta}2\ge\pi \). This gives a local, one-sided certificate that every zero in a window is simple and on the line. It needs the signs of Z, as Turing's method does, but no bound for S(t), no averaging over the ends of the window and no zero-free strip, and the kernel decays like \( e^{-\pi|x|/2} \), so that a window is self-contained. We ran it in ball arithmetic on windows of length 10 at heights \( 10^3 \) to \( 10^{15} \), and for Dirichlet L-functions. From the critical line only signs of Z are used, no values of \( |\zeta| \). The sign changes can be located in advance from the primes, as the crossings of the phase of the coefficient of the Hilbert problem computed from Müntz-smoothed sums. Nothing here bears on the Riemann hypothesis beyond the windows checked.
